AV: N (remote server, attacker controls it). Attack requires agent being connected to attacker's MCP server — a precondition: P. PR: attacker isn't authenticated to agent; they control remote server — PR N? The attacker is MCP operator; no privileges on agent needed. PR N. UI: user must ask to email the team — Passive (user uses system normally) — P. AC: L (manifest fetched automatically, shadowing straightforward). Impacts: email content exfiltrated — VC: agent process? Email content delivered to attacker: confidentiality of vulnerable system... The email content goes to attacker — integrity of email delivery (email never passes through agent's own tool): VI H? Email content disclosure = C. Subsequent systems: email intended recipients... Keep moderate: VC:L (email content the agent sends), VI:L, VA:N, SC:N, SI:L (recipients don't get email — integrity of their mailbox? actually email not sent — SI:L), SA:N.

AIVSS: LC: D — attacker-supplied description ("always use this") reaches tool invocation path without mediation? Description is attacker-controlled NL driving tool invocation — D (direct, no mediation). CP: N — no persistence across sessions (manifest refetched each run but not durable store... session context; no carryover). Could be N or S. Manifest is fetched each run but no durable store of attacker context — N. AP: C or N — influence relays from MCP server into tool dispatch under same principal? The remote server is a separate trust domain/operator... AP: L? Compromised intent crosses trust boundary into the agent from the MCP server — the attacker is already the MCP operator, an external party. AP: C — crosses components under same principal? The remote server is a subsequent system. I'd say AP: C (influence relays into agent's tool dispatch) — or L (crosses tenant/principal boundary: attacker's server → agent's principal). I'll pick C, contained within the agent. Hmm, the attacker is a different principal than the agent user; entry is via the MCP server which user connected. The propagation is into the agent (one component). AP: C.
